mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, it reduces the real discount rate, thereby increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 12-month pre-rate-change average (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified low-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite the defined labor-market signal, with a t-statistic below -1.5 in a 30-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend, sustained for two consecutive months, predicts rising business confidence and supply-chain activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > 2% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative and remain so for at least 10 consecutive such signals.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in consumer goods orders (not available in provided proxies; fallback: use INDPRO decline as proxy for supply shock) predicts near-term supply-side uncertainty, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >10% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified contraction (bootstrap p > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, it often prompts the Fed to signal tighter policy, which raises real discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in job openings (not available; fallback: use PAYEMS as proxy for labor absorption) predicts a labor market tightening that raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite the defined labor signal, with a t-statistic below -1.0 in a 40-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in retail sales proxy (not available; fallback: use GDPC1 as proxy for broad demand) for three months suggests weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by >2% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative during the identified demand decline (t-test p > 0.20).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and manufacturing activity (HOUST) both fall by more than 5% in the same month, it indicates a synchronized supply shock that elevates uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO down >5% AND HOUST down >5% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (bootstrap p > 0.30) during the identified disruption.
